option.approach: Investigate how nonadditivity of a quasitrace could produce arbitrarily long positive decompositions of the unit with large quasitrace on every summand. Determine what additional completeness or compactness argument would turn these into an infinite example.

options.counterfactual: No sequence satisfying the problem exists, despite the current assumption of nonemptiness; in fact, bounded positive partial sums always force the quasitraces of their individual summands to tend to zero.
options.approach: Try to prove directly that an infinite family of projections with bounded positive partial sums cannot have uniformly positive quasitrace. Spectral cutoffs of the proposed increments reduce the problem to precisely this assertion.
